title: Record S10's verification, fixes and hand-off
message:
Record S10's verification, fixes and hand-off

The Phase 10 record now holds the guide and screenshot work, the second
review's corrections, all fourteen fixes with their commits, the
building ablation, the verification on the final code (make test-all,
the help verifier, all 20 live gates, the 33-job CI matrix) and the
after-merge steps: the help sync, the deploy note for saved schedules,
and work item #11.

title: Document the autopilot and route-deletion rules in VESSEL_SYSTEM.md
message:
Document the autopilot and route-deletion rules in VESSEL_SYSTEM.md

The autopilot command table now gives pause and the real delwaypoint and delroute forms with the in-use refusals added in S10, and the autopilot section says why 'autopilot off' is refused under an NPC pilot. Ownership of shared waypoints and routes is GitLab work item #11.

title: Correct the guide from a second check against the code
message:
Correct the guide from a second check against the code

A fresh review of the finished guide against the code found rules the
guide stated too broadly or wrongly: who may give which orders and
where, what tenter, tgo and texit do on a vessel, when a ram strikes
and what a fitted ram adds, the crew's own repairs against
'shiprepair' at sea, the plunder and piracy conditions, the NPC
merchant bounty, docking range, grounding odds, raider boarding,
renown sharing, vehicle loading, event teams and scores, the wreck's
missing sails, and the summons' side effects. Captions now claim only
what each screenshot shows, and the staff lines left in shot 49 are
blanked. The guide also states the S10 fixes made since: scheduled
departures, 'autopilot off' under a pilot, shared waypoints and routes
in use, and boarding and docking by contact.

title: Find a boarding or docking target as shiplock does
message:
Find a boarding or docking target as shiplock does

board_hostile and dock took the first hull anywhere in the world whose
name had the word given, so beside a Corsair Ketch a room away,
'board_hostile ketch' could pick another Ketch out of sight and answer
"The target vessel is too far away!". Both now resolve the name as
shiplock and shipfire do, among the contacts: contact ID first, then a
word of the name, nearest first. find_ship_by_name(), left with no
caller, is removed with its test.

title: Keep shared waypoints and routes that a ship is using
message:
Keep shared waypoints and routes that a ship is using

Waypoints and routes belong to no one, and any captain could delete
any of them, the public ferry's loop and its waypoints included, which
stopped her scheduled departures. delwaypoint now refuses a waypoint
that a route sails through, and delroute a route that a hull runs on a
schedule or is sailing (under way, waiting or paused). Help says so in
both places.

title: Refuse 'autopilot off' while an NPC pilot holds the helm
message:
Refuse 'autopilot off' while an NPC pilot holds the helm

An assigned pilot engages a route the autopilot is off on, so 'autopilot
off' under a pilot printed "Autopilot disengaged." and half a second
later "The pilot engages autopilot.": the captain could not stop her.
The order is now refused with the two that hold, 'autopilot pause' and
'unassignpilot'. AUTOPILOT help says so in both places.

title: Keep scheduled departures on time across midnight
message:
Keep scheduled departures on time across midnight

A schedule's next departure was an hour of the day, (hour + interval)
% 24, and was due once the current hour was at least that: a six-hour
schedule set at hour 20 read hour 2 as already passed and departed
again at once, and an interval of 24 departed every hour. The next
departure is now an absolute MUD hour (schedule_mud_hour()); displays
show its hour of the day. A row saved in the old form reads as overdue
and departs once.

title: Read the test database switch once in the event test
message:
Read the test database switch once in the event test

clang-tidy's analyzer could not see that the second getenv() call
returns the same non-null value as the first, and flagged a possible
null argument to strcmp(). The test reads the switch once, as the other
DB-backed vessel tests do.

title: Add the illustrated Vessel Player Guide
message:
Add the illustrated Vessel Player Guide

docs/guides/VESSEL_PLAYER_GUIDE.md follows a new captain through the
vessel system in the order a player meets it: passage on public ships,
finding and buying a hull, crew and refits, sailing, routes, trade,
gunnery, damage and repair, prizes, other captains, contraband, loss and
recovery, other hulls and vehicles, the living world and client data,
with a command summary and a staff appendix. It is written from S9's
guide notes and screenshots, with every number and rule checked against
the code.

The screenshots move out of the temporary ongoing-projects folder to
docs/guides/vessel-guide/. Ten are cropped to the lines that matter and
four have staging lines or old interior minimaps blanked; three that
duplicate another shot or show something other than their note are
removed. The master index and VESSEL_SYSTEM.md link to the guide.

title: Record S10's audit, fact check and fixes so far
message: Record S10's audit, fact check and fixes so far

title: Bring VESSEL_SYSTEM.md's vehicle facts up to the code
message:
Bring VESSEL_SYSTEM.md's vehicle facts up to the code

The vehicle table gave a cart one passenger and 200 lbs (the code gives
two and 500) and was wrong for every type; the speed table varied by
type though one modifier per terrain applies to all; the terrain flags
listed a WATER_SHALLOW that does not exist and left out SWAMP;
unloadvehicle was shown taking a name (it takes a list number); and the
vessel-and-vehicle workflow mounted the vehicle before loading it,
which loadvehicle refuses. tenter's row now gives its optional target.

title: Correct vessel help that disagreed with the code
message:
Correct vessel help that disagreed with the code

S10's check of the guide's facts against the source found help that
says what the game does not do:
- SEASTATE: shallow water grounds a hull only at battle stations or with
  her crew stunned, not every deep-draft hull.
- VESSELS: an unowned hull with no pilot answers to anyone at her helm.
- SETSCHEDULE: no autopilot capability is required, only being aboard.
- ASSIGNPILOT: the pilot engages a set route only while the autopilot is
  off; a finished or paused route waits for 'autopilot on'.
- SHIPRAM: a rammer at least as heavy as her target slews it about; a
  lighter rammer is stopped dead.
- SHIPFIRE: no firing anywhere in port, nor with the crew stunned or
  reeling from a ram, not only at a berth.
- SHIPFIX: it also mends weapon damage and stops a sinking.

title: Never let the customs chance fall under 5 percent
message:
Never let the customs chance fall under 5 percent

Help promises customs a chance of never below 5 percent, and Duris's
own comment says "always a small chance", but like Duris the formula
floored only a negative chance: a renowned captain with a full hold
could carry contraband in at 0 to 4 percent. The chance is now never
under 5.

title: Widen shiplist's Class and Name columns
message:
Widen shiplist's Class and Name columns

shiplist cut "Magical Vessel" to "Magical Ve" and "Sablebranch Grand
Freighter" to 25 letters, the overflow S9 fixed in shipbrowse. The
Class column now holds 14 letters and the Name column 30.

title: Show a hull in her room as she lies, not always moored
message:
Show a hull in her room as she lies, not always moored

A hull's room line was written once, when she was placed or renamed,
and always read "is moored here": a captain thrown into the sea beside
his sinking ship read "Kestrel is moored here." Look now builds a
managed hull's line as she lies at that moment: moored at a berth or
alongside, at anchor, sinking, hovering overhead, or simply here. The
lookout gate's open-water observer now reads "Azure Watch is here".

title: Name event entrants and ghosts by contact ID
message:
Name event entrants and ghosts by contact ID

vevent told a captain "Entered Sea Wren (slot 13)", its status listed
entrants as "slot 16 Wren Skiff" and ghost ships as "Ghost contact:
slot 33": fleet slots are a builder's number, while every player
command names a hull by her contact ID. Entry, the roster and the ghost
contacts now show the contact ID ("[AN]"), which shiplock and shipfire
take. Staff enlistment still takes the slot.

title: Point tgo's hints at tgo and tenter
message:
Point tgo's hints at tgo and tenter

With no direction, tgo printed "Usage: go <north|...>", and outside a
transport it said "Try 'enter' to board a transport first.": go and
enter are other commands. The hints now name tgo and tenter.

title: Let tenter take the vehicle it names
message:
Let tenter take the vehicle it names

TENTER's help gives it a target, but the command read the argument and
ignored it, entering the first vehicle in the room: beside a cart and
a wagon, 'tenter wagon' climbed onto the cart. It now finds the vehicle
as VMOUNT does, refuses a name that matches none, and with no name
enters the transport here as before. Help says so in both places.

title: Tell a ship refused the shore that she keeps to the water
message:
Tell a ship refused the shore that she keeps to the water

A ship or warship steered at the beach or land, or ordered to climb,
was told "It requires deep water to sail", though shoal water is open
to her: S9's captain heard it in shoal water with land ahead. The
refusal now says she keeps to the water's surface, clear of beach and
land. The scale benchmark's terrain probe matches the new wording.

title: Keep the route when the NPC pilot is relieved
message:
Keep the route when the NPC pilot is relieved

unassignpilot on a hull sailing a route freed the route while the
autopilot still held it, so 'autopilot status' read freed memory and
'setroute', 'autopilot on' or the hull's cleanup could free it again
and crash the server. Relieving the pilot now disengages the autopilot
as 'autopilot off' does, and the route stays set for 'autopilot on'.
The DB-backed test relieves a pilot under way and sails the route on.

title: Plan S10: the illustrated player guide
